subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: What durable responsibility lifecycle and owner-confirmed reuse contract should OpenClaw support across memory, skills, actions, and evidence?
rationale: Automation cannot choose this safely because the answer defines public plugin/API shape, persisted state schema, security policy, user approval semantics, and operator configuration across multiple existing features.

options.title: Define a native minimal lifecycle contract first
options.body: Specify the owner-confirmed, review-passed, storage-confirmed, revoked, superseded, and reuse-policy state model before implementation, then extend storage and plugin seams only as needed.

options.title: Scope to narrower canonical issues
options.body: Keep #96675 as an umbrella and drive implementation through #7707, #48519, #54508, and #87714 so each surface gets a focused design and migration plan.

options.title: Defer to external integrations
options.body: Document SCBKR, UMP, AKF, or world-model-mcp as external prior art and wait for a concrete missing OpenClaw API before adding native lifecycle support.

recommendation.title: Define a native minimal lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the owner-confirmed, review-passed, storage-confirmed, revoked, superseded, and reuse-policy state model before implementation, then extend storage and plugin seams only as needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has strong feature-history signal around memory host SDK extraction, runtime/plugin contracts, and docs for the memory and session seams this decision would extend.
